devdoc.author: Tim Clancy <@_Enoch> This contract is meant to serve as an upgraded replacement for the original  BYTES contract in order to support tunable emissions from the new Neo Tokyo  staker. This contract maintains the requisite stubs to function with the rest  of the Neo Tokyo ecosystem. This contract also maintains the original admin  functions.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

decreaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically decreases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `spender` must have allowance for the caller of at least `subtractedValue`.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `amount`.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. This is not required by the EIP. See the note at the beginning of {ERC20}. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `amount`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `amount`.

devdoc.title: A migrated ERC-20 BYTES token contract for the Neo Tokyo ecosystem.

DoNotHaveEnoughOldBytes(uint256).notice: This error is thrown when a caller attempts to exchange more BYTES than they  hold.

BytesUpgraded(address,uint256).notice: This event is emitted when a caller upgrades their holdings of BYTES 1.0 to  the new BYTES 2.0 token.

ManagementUpdated(address,bytes32,bytes3.notice: An event emitted when a management relationship in `managerRight` is updated. This event captures adding and revoking management permissions via observing the update history of the `managerRight` value.

PermitUpdated(address,address,bytes32,by.notice: An event emitted when an address has a permit updated. This event captures, through its various parameter combinations, the cases of granting a permit, updating the expiration time of a permit, or revoking a permit.

ADMIN().notice: The identifier for the right to perform some contract changes.

BURN().notice: The identifier for the right to perform token burns.

BYTES1().notice: The address of the original BYTES 1.0 contract.

MANAGER().notice: A special constant specifying the unique manager right. This right allows an address to freely-manipulate the `managedRight` mapping.

S1_CITIZEN().notice: The address of the S1 Citizen contract.

STAKER().notice: The address of the Neo Tokyo staker contract.

TREASURY().notice: The address of the treasury which will receive minted DAO taxes.

UNIVERSAL().notice: A special constant specifying the unique, universal-rights circumstance.

ZERO_RIGHT().notice: A special reserved constant for representing no rights.

burn(address,uint256).notice: Permit authorized callers to burn BYTES from the `_from` address. When  BYTES are burnt, 2/3 of the BYTES burnt are minted to the DAO treasury. This  operation is never expected to overflow given operational bounds on the  amount of BYTES tokens ever allowed to enter circulation.

changeStakingContractAddress(address).notice: Allow a permitted caller to update the staker contract address.

changeTreasuryContractAddress(address).notice: Allow a permitted caller to update the treasury address.

constructor.notice: Construct a new instance of this BYTES 2.0 contract configured with the  given immutable contract addresses.

getReward(address).notice: This function is called by the S1 Citizen contract to emit BYTES to callers  based on their state from the staker contract.

hasRight(address,bytes32,bytes32).notice: Determine whether or not an address has some rights under the given circumstance,

hasRightUntil(address,bytes32,bytes32).notice: Determine whether or not an address has some rights under the given circumstance, and if they do have the right, until when.

managerRight(bytes32).notice: An additional mapping of managed rights to manager rights. This mapping represents the administrator relationship that various rights have with one another. An address with a manager right may freely set permits for that manager right's managed rights. Each right may be managed by only one other right.

permissions(address,bytes32,bytes32).notice: A mapping of per-address permissions to the circumstances, represented as an additional layer of generic bytes32 data, under which the addresses have various permits. A permit in this sense is represented by a per-circumstance mapping which couples some right, represented as a generic bytes32, to an expiration time wherein the right may no longer be exercised. An expiration time of 0 indicates that there is in fact no permit for the specified address to exercise the specified right under the specified circumstance.

setManagerRight(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Set the `_managerRight` whose `UNIVERSAL` holders may freely manage the specified `_managedRight`.

setPermit(address,bytes32,bytes32,uint25.notice: Set the permit to a specific address under some circumstances. A permit may only be set by the super-administrative contract owner or an address holding some delegated management permit.

updateReward(address,address,uint256).notice: This function is called by the S1 Citizen contract before an NFT transfer  and before a call to `getReward`. For historical reasons it must be left  here as a stub and cannot be entirely removed, though now it remains as a  no-op.

updateRewardOnMint(address,uint256).notice: This function is called by the S1 Citizen contract when a new citizen is  minted. For historical reasons it must be left here as a stub and cannot be  entirely removed, though now it remains as a no-op.

upgradeBytes(uint256).notice: Allow holders of the old BYTES contract to change them for BYTES 2.0; old  BYTES tokens will be burnt.
